gsp_control_detail.source_mapping: MAME stores the low control window in gsp_control_lo; its offset-zero value supplies the GSP VRAM expander color latch. The repeated words are address-space aliases observed through direct TMS34010 reads, not eight independent semantic fields.
gsp_control_detail.interpretation: The late drive path changes the GSP color latch after the input transition, providing a narrower rendering-state boundary. It is still not a semantic player-state selector.

new_drive_path_candidates.0xFFF45330: reads a word through A4 and writes it to @F4000000
new_drive_path_candidates.0xFFF479E0: builds a replicated byte value in B9 and writes it to @F4000000

gsp_trace_differential.interpretation: The drive trace adds two GSP-side F4000000 writer routines in the bounded post-start trace window. They are strong literal candidates for the changed renderer path, but trace instruction counts do not establish exact frame ownership or player-state semantics.

adsp_buffer_probe.interpretation: The late control transition adds no 68010 writes to the observed ADSP buffer window; this does not characterize ADSP-internal writes or other shared windows.

main_state_snapshot.observed: 0xFF9000-0xFF9003, 0xFF9004-0xFF9007, 0xFFDB4A, and 0xFFDAEE are identical at every sampled landmark in both schedules.
main_state_snapshot.interpretation: The statically identified input-adjacent record window is not sufficient as a late-control selector; the observed GSP and checkpoint divergence occurs through another state path.

interpretation: This is the strongest current candidate for a synchronized player-control boundary: late coin/start reaches a roadway state, and the verified drive schedule changes both the rendered result and machine/GSP state after a bounded delay. It remains a candidate rather than a semantic gameplay selector until the input transition and state fields are tied to ROM-side meaning.
